To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bradykinins can cause either a graded or an ‘all-or-none’ response in single tracheal smooth cells.
bradykinins induce changes in [Ca 2+]i of single bovine smooth muscle cells that can be mediated by a calcium influx and/or a calcium‐induced calcium release from intracellular calcium stores.
bradykinins can cause an increase in [ Ca2+]i in bovine trachealis cells, and that this effect is mediated by B2 receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and characterization of novel bradykinin receptor antagonists and with the identification of bradykinins and kinins in the respiratory tract and their possible role as autacoids in the regulation of the airways.
the development of new methods to measure the effects of drugs on single bovine trachial smooth muscle (BTM) cells.
the development and application of new methods for the investigation of the pharmacology of single smooth muscle cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in intracellular calcium ions in BTSM cells is a complex event involving both calcium influx and intracellular release.
the response to bradykinins in bovine trachea is mediated by the B2 receptor subtype and that the response is mediated via a calcium‐dependent mechanism.

bradykin‐induced increase of [Ca2+]in bovine trachea cells is mediated via bradykinin receptors, which are coupled to the release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores and to Ca2+ influx from extracellular space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bradykinins are involved in the control of [Ca2+] in BTSM cells.
the bradykinins can increase [Ca2+] in bovine trachea cells by two mechanisms, one of which is mediated by the B2 receptors and the other by a non‐receptor‐mediated mechanism.
bradykinins are able to induce an increase in [ Ca 2+] i in BTSM cells via a B 2 receptor and that this response may involve the activation of both extracellular‐ and intracellular‐mediated pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the increase in calcium ions is a graded process that is dependent on the concentration of brady-kinin.

bradykinins can be used to study intracellular calcium ion concentrations in individual BTSM cells.
